articles.title: In 1954, a Maryland family bought a worn-out 62-acre truck farm and let the land heal; 72 years later, Toad Hall is permanently protected inside a 1,200-acre conservation block
articles.summary: US News: In 1954, a Maryland family bought 62 acres of tired farmland and chose not to force it back into production. Instead, the property was given time to r.
articles.body: In 1954, a Maryland family bought 62 acres of tired farmland and chose not to force it back into production. Instead, the property was given time to recover, allowing fields, woods, wetlands and wildlife habitat to return gradually. Seventy-two years later, that patient decision has become part of a much larger conservation story. Toad Hall, a property in Kent County, Maryland, is now permanently protected through a conservation easement and forms part of a connected 1,200-acre conservation block. Reporting by Eastern Shore Undercover says the agreement also represents the 350th protected property completed by the conservation group involved. The achievement offers a reminder that environmental restoration does not always begin with a grand project. Sometimes, it starts when landowners decide to leave a worn-out piece of ground alone and allow nature to rebuild.A farm given time to recoverWhen the family purchased the property in 1954, Toad Hall was a 62-acre truck farm. The term “truck farm” refers to land used to grow vegetables and other crops for market. Like many working farms, the property had been shaped by years of cultivation, planting, harvesting and the constant pressure to produce.But instead of continuing to intensively farm every part of the land, the family allowed the property to heal. Over the decades, previously cultivated areas were given space to change. Vegetation returned, natural processes resumed and the landscape gradually became more valuable as habitat.That kind of recovery can be easy to overlook. It does not always involve a dramatic rewilding project, a large-scale planting campaign or a sudden transformation visible from one day to the next. Often, it happens slowly: a field is no longer ploughed, native plants spread, trees mature, water moves through the land more naturally and animals begin using the area again.Toad Hall’s story is therefore rooted in patience. The family’s decision to let the land rest created the foundation for its protection many decades later.From private land to permanent protectionThe property’s future changed when it became protected through a conservation easement. A conservation easement is a legal agreement that permanently limits certain types of development on private land. The land can remain privately owned, but its conservation values are protected for the future.This arrangement allows landowners to care for their property while ensuring that important natural features are not lost to subdivision or intensive development. Depending on the agreement, farming, forestry or other compatible activities may continue, but large-scale development is restricted.For Toad Hall, the easement means the 62 acres will remain protected permanently. The decision does not simply preserve the property as it looks today. It protects the land’s ecological potential, including its ability to provide habitat, store water, support native plants and form part of a larger connected landscape.That long-term legal protection matters because ownership can change. Families may eventually sell or transfer land, and economic pressures can alter the way a property is used. A conservation easement creates a safeguard that remains in place even when the people connected to the property change.The importance of a connected landscapeToad Hall is not an isolated patch of protected land. It sits within a 1,200-acre conservation block, making the agreement significant beyond the property’s boundaries.Wildlife does not recognise property lines. Birds, mammals, insects and amphibians move between feeding areas, nesting sites, wetlands, forests and fields. When protected parcels are connected, animals have more space to move and plants have a better chance of spreading.Large, connected conservation areas can also help ecosystems cope with change. A species that loses access to one part of its habitat may be able to relocate to another. Natural areas can provide refuge during storms, droughts, heatwaves and other environmental stresses.For plants and animals, a 1,200-acre block is more useful than a collection of tiny, disconnected islands. Roads, buildings and intensive land use can divide habitats, making it harder for wildlife to travel safely and reducing the genetic exchange between populations.By adding Toad Hall to the protected landscape, the easement strengthens the wider block. The property becomes one more piece of a natural network rather than a solitary island of habitat.Why farmland can become wildlife habitatAgricultural land is not automatically hostile to wildlife. Much depends on how it is managed and what happens when intensive cultivation stops.Former farm fields can develop into grassland, shrubland or young woodland. These habitats may support pollinators, songbirds, small mammals and reptiles. Older trees can provide nesting cavities, while fallen branches and leaf litter create shelter for insects and other small organisms.Wet areas and drainage channels can also become important habitat. They may hold water during rainy periods, filter runoff and provide breeding areas for amphibians. Vegetated edges between fields and woods can offer cover for animals moving across the landscape.The transformation is not always neat or predictable. A recovering property may look overgrown to some people, but what appears untidy can be ecologically productive. Dead trees, fallen leaves, native weeds and dense undergrowth all contribute to a functioning ecosystem.Toad Hall illustrates how land can acquire new value over time. It began as a working farm, but its importance now includes the natural systems that developed after the soil was allowed to rest.A milestone for conservationThe conservation agreement is also notable because it became the 350th protected property completed by the organisation involved, according to Eastern Shore Undercover.That milestone represents more than a number. Each protected property requires landowner participation, legal work, funding, planning and long-term stewardship. The properties may differ in size and character, but together they create a record of local decisions made in favour of conservation.The 350th easement also reflects changing attitudes towards private land. Conservation is often associated with national parks, public forests or government-owned reserves. Yet a significant amount of habitat exists on privately owned land.Landowners can play a vital role in protecting open space, maintaining wildlife corridors and preventing development in ecologically important areas. Their decisions can influence water quality, biodiversity and the visual character of an entire region.In this case, the original family’s decision to let the land recover was followed decades later by a formal agreement that secured its future. The two choices—first allowing nature to return, then protecting the property legally—work together.The value of patienceEnvironmental restoration is often discussed in terms of targets and deadlines. Projects may promise to plant a certain number of trees, restore a particular wetland area or protect a specific amount of land. Those goals are important, but Toad Hall’s history highlights another ingredient: time.Seventy-two years passed between the family’s purchase of the farm and the property’s permanent protection. During that period, the land was able to develop gradually. Trees grew, soils changed and habitat matured.Nature rarely follows a quick schedule. A newly planted woodland may take decades to resemble a mature forest. A recovering field may pass through several stages before becoming suitable for the species that conservationists hope to support. Some ecological benefits may not be obvious until many years after a management decision is made.The story also shows why conservation should look beyond immediate results. A property that seems unremarkable today may become increasingly valuable as surrounding areas are developed. Protecting it early can prevent the loss of options later.Protecting more than sceneryConservation easements are often praised for preserving scenic open space, and Toad Hall may certainly contribute to the rural character of Kent County. But protected land provides services that extend beyond what people see.Healthy vegetation can reduce soil erosion and slow the movement of rainwater. Wetlands and low-lying areas can help absorb excess water. Trees store carbon, offer shade and improve local habitat conditions. Diverse plant communities support pollinators and other organisms that contribute to healthy ecosystems.Protected land can also support education, research and outdoor recreation when appropriate access is available. Even where public entry is limited, the ecological benefits can extend beyond the property itself.These functions become especially important as communities grow. Development can replace fields, woods and wetlands with roads, rooftops and other hard surfaces. Once natural areas are fragmented or destroyed, restoring them is often expensive and difficult.Permanent protection provides a form of insurance. It keeps the land available for wildlife and natural processes, even as the surrounding region changes.A quiet conservation legacyToad Hall’s story does not centre on a famous species or a dramatic rescue. It is about a family, a piece of farmland and a decision to allow the landscape to recover.That quiet approach may be one of the most meaningful aspects of the property’s history. The land was not required to prove its value immediately. It was allowed to exist, change and mature. Years later, its importance was recognised through permanent protection.The property now contributes to a much larger 1,200-acre conservation block, while its easement marks the 350th protected property completed by the conservation group. Together, those facts place one family’s long-term relationship with the land inside a broader regional effort to preserve open space and habitat.Toad Hall shows that conservation can begin with restraint. Sometimes, the most powerful action is to stop disturbing the land and give it time. With legal protection added at the right moment, that patience can become a legacy—one capable of supporting wildlife and natural systems for generations to come.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'Utter disregard of human rights': Kashmiri activist slams Pak at UNHRC over PoK protest crackdown
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Kashmiri socio-political activist Tasleema Akhtar has raised concerns over the treatment of people in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir (.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Kashmiri socio-political activist Tasleema Akhtar has raised concerns over the treatment of people in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoJK), alleging that Pakistan has failed to protect their basic rights and provide adequate infrastructure and essential services.Addressing the 54th session of the UN human rights council in Geneva, Akhtar contrasted the situation in PoK with developments in the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir (JKUT). She alleged that people in PoK were living at the mercy of the Pakistan government amid poor infrastructure, limited investment and disregard for their basic rights.Her remarks come against the backdrop of concerns raised at the UNHRC over the human rights situation in PoK and Pakistan-occupied Gilgit-Baltistan.At the 63rd session of the council, United Kashmir People’s National Party chairman Sardar Shaukat Ali Kashmiri had alleged intensified repression in PoK since June 5 citing reports of arrests, violence, deaths, injuries, alleged disappearances and restrictions on internet and mobile communications.Kashmiri had called for an independent investigation into the reported violations and urged Pakistan to stop using force against peaceful protesters.'Strategic developmental differences'Akhtar told the UNHRC that there were significant differences in development between JKUT and PoJK.“Mr Vice President, being a native to J&K through UNHR Council, I would like to bring forth the strategic developmental differences of Union Territory of J&K, i.e. JKUT and Pak Occupied J&K.”She said the Indian government was investing in infrastructure and development projects in Jammu and Kashmir, while alleging that PoJK faced inadequate investment and misuse of its resources.“While JKUT is bringing transformational changes for the betterment of the region, people of POJK are living at the mercy of Pakistan Government having uttered disregard for the people over there and their basic human rights and amenities.”Akhtar also alleged that Pakistan was struggling with its financial obligations while shielding terrorist outfits involved in what she described as a proxy war against India.“While the Government of India is investing in infrastructure and developmental projects in J&K besides bringing peace and prosperity to the region, Pakistan is struggling to meet its basic financial obligations and is shielding terrorist outfitters to wage a proxy war against India.”Education concernsAkhtar highlighted education as one of the key areas where she said JKUT had an advantage over PoK.“PoK lacks even basic infrastructure and amenities, with negligible investment and built-in misappropriation of its resources by Pakistan. In terms of education and literacy rate, JKUT is far ahead of PoK. Government of India spends nine times more on education in JKUT compared to its counterpart.”She alleged that schools in PoK lacked basic facilities such as buildings, roofs, clean water and toilets. These shortcomings, she said, were creating hardships for students and contributing to a high dropout rate.“PoK is facing a major crisis in its education sector, lacking basic infrastructure including building and roofs, clean water, toilets, etc., causing acute hardships to students, resulting in severe drop-out ratio.”Healthcare accessAkhtar also pointed to differences in access to healthcare. She said people in JKUT were able to access health benefits under national schemes even in remote areas, while similar access remained a distant prospect for people in PoJK.“Change is also possible in health sector. PoK of health, UT are availing health benefits in even their remote areas with national health schemes, which is a distant dream for the people of PoK.”She further highlighted the government's health insurance coverage in Jammu and Kashmir.“Government of India facilitates people of the Juman Kashmir with universal health insurance coverage of far-reaching... Thank you.”Broader concerns over PoKAkhtar’s remarks followed wider concerns raised at the UNHRC over alleged restrictions and human rights violations in the Pakistan-occupied parts of Jammu and Kashmir.Kashmiri, while addressing the council’s 63rd session under Agenda Item 4, had called for independent monitoring of PoK and PoGB, an investigation into reported violations and the release of people he described as arbitrarily detained.“Peaceful dissent is not terrorism, and demanding rights is not a crime,” Kashmiri said.He also called for the whereabouts of missing people to be established and for unrestricted internet and mobile communications to be restored across PoK.“The Council must act now to safeguard the lives and fundamental rights of millions of Kashmiris,” he said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.body: MUMBAI: Maharashtra FDA Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe said he shared President Droupadi Murmu’s appeal to popular film artists not to endorse products harmful to people's health.Celebrities have a powerful influence on young minds and a true “star” should spread light, not darkness, Murmu said while addressing the 72nd National Film Awards ceremony on Tuesday.“Influence is not immunity. Artists, like everyone else, must respect the law and recognise the responsibility that comes with endorsing products, behaviours and habits that shape public choices,” Mundhe said on X.“When influence is used to endorse food products, public health cannot be an afterthought. No commercial interest can take precedence over public health,” Mundhe said.On August 11, the FDA issued notices to Bollywood actors Shah Rukh Khan, Ajay Devgn and Tiger Shroff, claiming that the Vimal Elaichi advertisement featuring them amounted to surrogate promotion of Vimal Pan Masala, a product prohibited in Maharashtra.The actors were instructed to immediately discontinue their participation, remove the advertisements from their social media and digital platforms and cease further promotional cooperation.(With inputs from PTI)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mumbai | Silver Rate in Mumbai | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Public Holidays in Mumbai | Mumbai AQI | Weather in Mumbai | Petrol Price in Mumbai | Diesel Price in Mumbai | CNG Price in Mumbai | LPG Price in MumbaiStay updated with the latest Mumbai news. articles.title: Brigitte Bardot’s 285 personal belongings were expected to bring about €50,000 at a Paris auction; instead, they fetched €953,531, nearly 20 times the estimate, as her widower criticised the sale
articles.summary: Rest of World News: French actress and singer Brigitte Bardot's personal items have fetched about €1 million at auction in Paris. The amount is almost 20 times the estima.
articles.body: French actress and singer Brigitte Bardot's personal items have fetched about €1 million at auction in Paris. The amount is almost 20 times the estimate, according to the auction house Millon. A total of 285 objects, ranging from straw hats, sunglasses and nightgowns to tableware and furniture from Bardot’s homes in Paris and Saint-Tropez, were auctioned, Agence France-Presse (AFP) reported.Two dog collars, with an ID tag bearing Bardot’s name and a telephone number, estimated at €30 for the pair, were sold for €9,400 to a Russian buyer. A self-portrait fetched nearly €40,000 while the typewriter she used to write an autobiography raised €4,634. Estimated at between €300 and €500, two of her guitars soared to €8,600 and €1,900, while three stuffed toys representing baby seals sold for nearly €2,200.About 3,000 French and international bidders registered for the auction. “Brigitte Bardot has once again proved to be a remarkable alchemist: she transformed about €50,000 in estimates into nearly €1m, including fees,” the auctioneer Alexandre Millon said.Bardot, who died in December 2025 at the age of 91, later transitioned into an animal rights activist in her career. She became famous through the film "And God Created Woman," in which she played a woman who confidently embraced her desires. This was considered scandalous at the time and therefore fascinated many viewers all the more. Until the early 1970s, Bardot appeared in approximately 50 films. She was one of the most photographed women in the world at that time.In 1973, Bardot gave up her acting career and dedicated her life to endangered animals. She auctioned off parts of her possessions to establish her animal welfare foundation. She also became increasingly active politically on the far right, alienating some fans in her later life with her hardline views on immigration. Bardot was convicted five times for hate speech, particularly about Muslims, and up until her death she expressed her pleasure at the rising share of the vote gained by the anti-immigration National Rally party.The proceeds from the auction will go to her animal welfare foundation and to Nicolas-Jacques Charrier, her only child. Founded by the actor in 1986, the Brigitte Bardot Foundation says it has taken in 13,000 animals through four shelters and 150 partner facilities, supports 350 groups in France and operates in 70 countries.“This sale is the logical continuation of the one she herself organised in 1987 with her most precious belongings to create her foundation,” Ghyslaine Calmels-Bock, the managing director of the Bardot Foundation, told AFP after the sale. “Today, her fight continues through this auction.”A 'joke' that turned wrong Two days before the auction, Bardot’s last husband, Bernard d’Ormale, described it as a “joke”. “These are personal items,” he said. “Why hold this sale? For the animals?” He said it amounted to a “disrespect to Brigitte’s memory”. Her belongings should have been preserved as part of her legacy, he told AFP, adding that Bardot “would not have agreed to this sale”.The foundation rejected the criticism, saying the auction had been approved by the board in June when the widower was its president. D’Ormale said he had not understood the auction would involve such personal items. The dispute comes days after he was removed as head of the foundation, a role he had held since Bardot’s death.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: 'Arrest poll panel chief': Mamata Banerjee demands repoll in Bengal amid EC 'SIR split' row
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee on Wednesday demanded fresh Assembly elections in West Bengal using the pre-Special Inten.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee on Wednesday demanded fresh Assembly elections in West Bengal using the pre-Special Intensive Revision (SIR) voter list while announcing pan-India protests against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, after a report claimed two Election Commissioners had raised objections to aspects of the voter-roll revision exercise.Reacting to a media report, Mamata demanded Kumar's arrest and accused the Election Commission of working in favour of the BJP."Re-election must be held in West Bengal with the old voter list," Banerjee said during a Facebook Live, adding that there would be "pan-India protests till Gyanesh Kumar remains CEC". "It has now been proven that the BJP and the EC looted the West Bengal assembly polls," she alleged.Mamata also called for Kumar to be arrested, saying, "He must be immediately arrested and put behind bars. The chair of the CEC is not for a person like him.""This is such a scandalous story. We had never seen this in our lives. This Election Commissioner must be arrested. He has no moral authority to continue," she said, referring to the report.The TMC leader said INDIA bloc partners had discussed the issue and would meet soon.Meanwhile, in another TMC pushback, national general secretary and MP Abhishek Banerjee separately accused the election commission of deliberately deleting 30 lakh voter names from West Bengal electoral rolls to benefit the BJP. He alleged that similar manipulation had taken place in Haryana and Bihar and demanded the immediate arrest of Kumar."The allegations we raised earlier have today been echoed by the other Election Commissioners as well. Just as the names of 30 lakh people were deleted from the voter list to benefit one political party, the same was done in Haryana and Bihar," Abhishek alleged.Abhishek also questioned the process through which Kumar was appointed, citing a split Supreme Court verdict on the Election Commission selection panel and the dismissal of an impeachment motion moved by Opposition parties.The Election Commission, however, said that "operational queries or inputs" had been raised by Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi on matters including the SIR exercise, but maintained that these related to the draft stage and were part of "standard administrative practice aimed at safeguarding voter rights". The poll panel also said decisions relating to the SIR were taken unanimously with the approval of all three Election Commissioners.The row erupted when a media report claimed that Sandhu and Joshi had formally objected at least 14 times over the past 10 months to decisions and orders concerning the SIR, including some that they allegedly said were taken without their knowledge.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Bihar, Maharashtra, Delhi, Haryana & West Bengal': Oppn seeks fresh polls after EC 'dissent' report
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav on Wednesday accused the Election Commission of being misused to benefit the BJP and alleged that election rules had
articles.body: NEW DELHI: RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav on Wednesday accused the Election Commission of being misused to benefit the BJP and alleged that election rules had been changed to weaken the Opposition’s ability to challenge poll results.At a press conference, Tejashwi questioned the functioning of the poll panel, raised concerns over changes to the retention period for voting and counting records, and demanded fresh elections in Bihar and Bengal. He also called for the removal of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.“Whether it is the results in Bihar or Maharashtra, Delhi, Haryana, or Bengal—the opposition has not lost. Rather, in these states, the EC has been misused to ensure that the BJP wins,” he said.He alleged that Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah had “flouted all the rules” and claimed the CEC had acted according to their wishes.“And this process is still continuing. It is going on in several states, and it is being carried out arbitrarily. There are objections from two Election Commissioners as well. Even then, neither Modi ji nor Amit Shah ji is coming forward and saying anything about it,” he said.He also questioned the change in the period for retaining voting and counting records. He said the earlier period of up to one year had been reduced to 45 days.“That means, when there is no evidence left, what can the opposition do? When they go to court, there will be no evidence, so there will be no benefit,” he said.On the appointment of the CEC, Tejashwi said the earlier selection panel included the Chief Justice of India, while a Union minister is now part of the panel.“This means that, as Modi ji wishes, one Gyanesh ji may be removed, but the BJP can bring in another Gyanesh Kumar,” he said.He also alleged that elections in Bihar and Bengal had been illegal and demanded fresh polls in both states.Stalin and Rahul hit out at ECLeader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi also hit out at the Election Commission over the alleged irregularities, calling “vote chori” a crime against Indian voters and an attack on the Constitution.“Vote chori is a crime against the Indian people and a direct attack on our constitution. The BJP, RSS and EC who organised it have committed an act of treason. Justice will be served,” he said.DMK supremo and former Tamil Nadu chief minister MK Stalin also demanded the removal of CEC Gyanesh Kumar. He cited allegations over the functioning of the EC during the special intensive revision of electoral rolls.Stalin said the DMK and other opposition parties had opposed the deletion of voters from electoral rolls under the SIR exercise. He said the process, carried out months before elections in different states, had faced allegations of irregularities, particularly in West Bengal.He said, "The Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam, along with other Opposition parties, has consistently opposed the move to delete crores of voters from the electoral rolls in the name of the Special Intensive Revision (#SIR). Rushed through just months ahead of elections in State after State, the exercise was riddled with irregularities and sparked widespread unrest, particularly in West Bengal."Stalin said the reported objections by election commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi over decisions related to SIR raised questions about the functioning of the three-member poll panel. Responding to a report by the Indian Express, he claimed the two commissioners had been kept unaware of key decisions and that their objections had been brushed aside on 14 occasions in 10 months."Gyanesh Kumar had been acting unilaterally and in secrecy, without the concurrence of the other two election commissioners. Even more alarming is the revelation that Thiru. Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Thiru."Stalin said the EC's decisions should follow the majority view when its members disagree. He argued that concerns raised by two serving commissioners could not be treated merely as an internal or procedural issue."Where the commissioners differ in opinion on any matter, the decision must be based on the majority view. If two of its three members were themselves kept unaware of what was being done in the commission’s name, this cannot be dismissed as a mere internal or procedural matter. It constitutes a grave assault on Indian democracy," he said.The DMK chief also raised questions over electoral-roll appeals filed even after courts had directed that certain voters be added to the rolls. He questioned who authorised and filed such appeals.Stalin said the party had earlier moved an impeachment motion against Gyanesh Kumar and demanded that he step down.“Gyanesh Kumar must go immediately. The SIR exercise must be halted,” Stalin said, while calling for a “fair and thorough investigation” into the functioning of the Election Commission.Mamata Banerjee calls report ‘scandalous’Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee also attacked the Election Commission over the reported objections by the two commissioners to decisions linked to the SIR process.Reacting to the Indian Express report, Mamata alleged that the poll panel had been misused and demanded action against Gyanesh Kumar.“This is such a scandalous story. We had never seen this in our lives. This election commissioner must be arrested. He has no moral authority to continue, and BJP must see that they cannot destroy our Constitution. They cannot demolish democracy,” she said.Mamata also alleged that people linked to the BJP had been deployed in the electoral-roll process and accused the CEC of misusing the police.“They cannot depute their own EROs in the name of BJP IT Team. What we said earlier has now been exposed,” she said.She further said, “Gyanesh Kumar has misused Police and with BJP they have deputed their own BJP-minded people. Such a scandal has never happened. If you have any honour, you yourself would ask to be arrested. You should be arrested.”Akhilesh Yadav questions poll panel’s functioningSamajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav also questioned the functioning of the Election Commission, saying the reported objections by two election commissioners had raised serious concerns over the poll panel's impartiality.Addressing a press conference in Lucknow, Akhilesh referred to reports that Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had recorded objections 14 times over 10 months to decisions and orders concerning SIR and electoral-roll procedures.“This is dangerous for our democracy. This is an attempt to weaken our democracy,” he said.Akhilesh questioned whether elections held during a period when the Election Commission was allegedly not acting impartially could be considered fair.“This means that the governments which have been formed during this period are unconstitutional governments,” he said.In an earlier post on X, he described the reported objections by the two commissioners as “extremely serious news” and urged the Supreme Court to take suo motu cognisance of the matter.He also alleged that voters supporting the Samajwadi Party had been systematically removed from electoral rolls and claimed that no action was taken despite the party bringing the matter to the Election Commission's notice.“Samajwadi Party voters were systematically deleted from the Election Commission's voters list. We brought this to the notice of the Election Commission, but no action was taken against anyone. Rampant malpractice was committed on a massive scale in the by-elections,” he said.The EC has rejected the suggestion that its decisions were taken without the participation of all three commissioners. It said decisions, including those related to SIR, were taken unanimously with the approval of the CEC and the two other election commissioners.The poll panel said written notes, observations, technical suggestions and internal checks were standard practices within a multi-member constitutional body. It said differing views were part of institutional deliberations before final decisions were taken and that all official orders had legal sanction and followed established procedures.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Nandigram bypoll: Congress candidate Milan Pradhan sent to judicial custody till October 7
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: A court in West Bengal's Purba Medinipur district on Wednesday sent Milan Pradhan, the Congress' candidate for the upcoming Nandigram bypol.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A court in West Bengal's Purba Medinipur district on Wednesday sent Milan Pradhan, the Congress' candidate for the upcoming Nandigram bypoll, to judicial custody until October 7, a day after voting, in connection with a 2007 criminal case.The Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate of Contai Court remanded Pradhan to judicial custody after the prosecution sought his custody in connection with a murder charge.Pradhan, who was already in judicial custody until October 5 in a separate Arms Act case, was arraigned on murder and other charges in connection with a case also registered in 2007 during the Nandigram anti-land acquisition movement, his lawyer, Prasenjit Jana, said.The court rejected the Congress candidate's bail plea, Jana added.The order effectively ended Pradhan's chances of campaigning for the byelection, as campaigning is scheduled to conclude on October 4. The counting of votes will be held on October 9.Congress moves Calcutta HC against Pradhan's arrestEarlier in the day, the Congress said it had moved the Calcutta high court seeking bail for Pradhan. The high court agreed to hear the matter on Thursday. The West Bengal government did not mention this case during a hearing on September 22.Pradhan's advocate, Ayan Bhattacharjee, mentioned the matter before Justice Sauagata Bhattacharyya, submitting that the Congress candidate had been shown as arrested and produced before the court for remand in the case.Justice Bhattacharyya on Tuesday verbally asked the West Bengal government's counsel to allow Pradhan to contest the Nandigram byelection, provided he gets bail in the five criminal cases in which he has been arrested.Pradhan's arrest on September 18 came just hours after Mamata Banerjee announced that her faction of the Trinamool Congress would support the Congress candidate in Nandigram, after its nominee, Sanchita Pradhan De, withdrew from the contest.The following day, he was sent to judicial custody by the Haldia sub-divisional court until October 3 in connection with four other pending non-bailable arrest warrants linked to cases in Nandigram dating back to 2007.Several criminal cases were registered against Pradhan in 2007 at police stations in Nandigram and Khejuri in Purba Medinipur district.During a hearing on an application filed by him seeking protection from coercive action in six other cases registered against him, the state on Tuesday informed the High Court that five of them had been withdrawn by the previous government and that he was not wanted in the sixth case.The high court was informed on Tuesday that Pradhan had been arrested and sent to judicial remand in connection with the other five criminal cases.The October 6 bypoll to the Nandigram Assembly seat was necessitated after chief minister Suvendu Adhikari vacated the constituency and retained Mamata Banerjee's erstwhile stronghold of Bhabanipur. He won both seats in the assembly polls held earlier this year. The BJP won the assembly elections to form its first government in the state, while the TMC was voted out after 15 years.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Cyclone Arnab: Why the name is trending as Odisha braces for a deep depression near the coast
articles.summary: BHUBANESWAR: Odisha’s Malkangiri district has stepped up disaster preparedness as a depression over the Bay of Bengal moves towards the north Andhra
articles.body: BHUBANESWAR: Odisha’s Malkangiri district has stepped up disaster preparedness as a depression over the Bay of Bengal moves towards the north Andhra Pradesh-south Odisha coast, with authorities putting rescue teams on standby, opening cyclone shelters and deploying heavy machinery in vulnerable areas.According to news agency ANI, Malkangiri administration has intensified preparations ahead of the system’s expected landfall, with the district targeting “zero casualties”. Collector Prathamesh Arvind Rajeshirke said heavy rainfall was expected to intensify from Wednesday evening and continue through Thursday morning.‘Calm before the storm’Several parts of the district have already received significant rainfall. Khairput and Mathili blocks recorded more than 60mm and 80mm of rain respectively, while the district’s cumulative rainfall remained below 350mm, the collector told ANI.The district had experienced a temporary lull in rain since 6am on Wednesday, but Rajeshirke described it as potentially the “calm before the storm”, with heavier showers expected later in the day.Authorities are keeping a close watch on low-lying areas and water bodies, particularly after four bridges were submerged during heavy rain around two weeks ago.Barricades have now been placed around three to four vulnerable bridges to prevent people and vehicles from entering potentially dangerous stretches.220 JCBs readyAs per the ANI report, the administration has deployed around 220 JCB excavators in valley and ghat areas to tackle landslides and ensure roads can be cleared quickly if debris blocks key routes.Two teams of the Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force, or ODRAF, have also been moved from Koraput. One team has been positioned in Mathili and Govindpalli, while the other has been stationed in Kalimela.Cyclone shelters have been made operational in case evacuation becomes necessary. Officials have also arranged dry rations and cooked food for people who may need to be moved to safer locations.Schools and Anganwadi centres in the district have been given holidays, while leave granted to government officials has been cancelled.The state administration has also been holding preparedness meetings, with senior officials reviewing response plans and directing departments to coordinate rescue and relief operations.What IMD saysThe weather system over the Bay of Bengal is currently a depression and not an officially named cyclone.The India Meteorological Department has forecast that the system could strengthen into a deep depression as it moves west-northwestwards. It is expected to cross the north Andhra Pradesh-south Odisha coast between Visakhapatnam and Gopalpur during the night of September 23 and the early hours of September 24.Heavy to very heavy rainfall has been forecast across parts of southern and coastal Odisha, with isolated extremely heavy rain also possible.The IMD has issued a red alert for several southern Odisha districts during September 23-25. Koraput, Gajapati and Ganjam are expected to see heavy to very heavy rainfall on September 23 and 24, while Kalahandi, Nabarangpur, Koraput and Malkangiri are under red alert for September 24 and 25.Squally winds, with gusts of up to 75 kmph, are also expected along and off the south Odisha-north Andhra Pradesh coast through September 24.Why ‘Cyclone Arnab’ is being discussedThe weather system has also sparked curiosity around the name “Cyclone Arnab”, but that does not mean the current depression has officially been named Arnab.Under the North Indian Ocean cyclone-naming system, tropical cyclones are assigned names from a predetermined regional list maintained through the WMO/ESCAP Panel on Tropical Cyclones. Arnab, contributed by Bangladesh, is one of the names on that list.However, a weather system is given a cyclone name only after it reaches the prescribed intensity for a tropical cyclone. The present system has not reached that stage, with the IMD currently forecasting intensification into a deep depression.Therefore, “Arnab” is best understood as the next relevant name in the regional roster, rather than the official name of the system currently approaching Odisha.Odisha districts brace for heavy rainThe approaching system has already prompted precautionary measures across Odisha. Several districts have shut schools and Anganwadi centres as heavy rain lashed parts of the state.Schools in Khurda, Jagatsinghpur, Ganjam and Gajapati were closed, while Malkangiri ordered schools to remain shut until September 24.The state government has placed collectors of 11 districts on high alert and kept cyclone and flood shelters ready amid the possibility of waterlogging, urban flooding, landslides and mudslides.Authorities have also restricted movement on vulnerable stretches, including Kalinga Ghat, while ferry services between Satapada and Jahnikuda in Chilika Lake have been suspended until September 25.For now, the focus remains on the deep depression, its expected movement towards the Odisha-Andhra coast and the heavy rain threat. Whether the system eventually reaches cyclone intensity, and whether the name Arnab becomes applicable, will depend on its subsequent development as monitored by the IMD.(With agency inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Bhubaneswar | Silver Rate in Bhubaneswar | Bank Holidays in Bhubaneswar | Public Holidays in Bhubaneswar | Petrol Price in Bhubaneswar | Diesel Price in Bhubaneswar | CNG Price in Bhubaneswar | LPG Price in BhubaneswarStay updated with the latest Bhubaneswar news. articles.title: F-35, Rafale, Tejas in one battlespace: Tarang Shakti brings the world's air power to India
articles.summary: The Indian Air Force is set to host the second edition of Tarang Shakti, its biggest multilateral air exercise yet.
articles.body: The Indian Air Force is set to host the second edition of Tarang Shakti, its biggest multilateral air exercise yet. The exercise is being held at the Jodhpur air base from September 26 to October 11, bringing together nearly 40 air forces including those from the United States, France and Germany. The exercise, conducted in the backdrop of lessons drawn from Operation Sindoor last year, will see fighter jets, transport aircraft and specialist assets from partner air forces operate alongside the IAF in a realistic combat environment, with officials describing it as a platform to test tactics, procedures and interoperability among friendly forces.Tarang Shakti: Full spectrum of aerial warfare and beyondThe primary reason for holding Exercise Tarang Shakti is to improve military interoperability, share operational best practices, and strengthen strategic defense partnerships among global air forces. Hosted by the Indian Air Force (IAF), it serves as India's largest multinational air combat exercise, moving beyond traditional bilateral drills to foster collective security and cooperation. The exercise allows pilots and ground crews from multiple nations to fly, communicate, and coordinate complex tactical maneuvers together, bridging differences in work cultures and combat philosophies.Participants test combat assumptions and exchange real-world lessons from modern air warfare environments, refining joint counter-air, air defense, and reconnaissance strategies. Promoting indigenous capabilities as it provides a major global platform for India to showcase its domestically manufactured defense equipment—such as the LCA Tejas, ALH Dhruv and LCH Prachand. Thus demonstrating to the visiting air forces the country's booming indigenous aviation ecosystem. The IAF's top of the line Rafale fighter aircraft will also be participating in the exercise.By bringing together dozens of participating and observing nations, multinational wargames also provide an opportunity to extend defence diplomacy to members of participating nations through peer-to-peer connect. Such relationships help foster better understanding and paves way for greater cooperation in the future.A key element of such exercises is Dissimilar Air Combat Training (DACT), where aircraft of different types and origins are pitted against each other rather than against similar platforms. This allows pilots to understand the strengths and weaknesses of unfamiliar aircraft, through which pilots learn to adapt and overcome. This helps in sharpening tactics against adversary-type jets, and prepare for scenarios where the enemy may be flying something entirely different from what they train against at home.Another advantage of hosting these exercises is that the IAF gets to test its Tactics, Techniques and Procedures (TTP) against a force that has formulated its own set of strategy that have evolved from a different type of presumptions and threat environment. An exercise of such nature allows participating air forces and especially the hosting air force to execute, validate and perform a gap analysis of its own TTPs, thereby strengthening them. As the hosting air force sets the ground rules for the entire exercise can be tailored to test and improve the air force's war fighting plans.More, on the ground level, hosting an international exercise of this nature opens up for cross pollination of best practices the entire operational gamut of aerial operations. When IAF goes out for an exercise abroad, it is only the pilots and a limited number of crew who get exposed to the newest and best practices followed by other air forces. While hosting the exercise at home, a much larger number of IAF personnel get exposed to the practices followed by other air arms, who to learn from the IAF.The F-35 in the Indian skiesThe presence of the American F-35 is expected to be one of the biggest draws of this edition. Unlike the previous two appearances at aero-shows in Bengaluru, this will be the jet's first outing in a military exercise on Indian soil. Last year an F-35 of the UK's Royal Navy was stranded at the Thiruvananthapuram Airport for 37 days after it developed a snag. But this is the first time that the aircraft will show-off its combat capabilities in an operational scenario over the sub-continent.The F-35A is the most advanced fighter aircraft in service today. The aircraft, designed to be nearly invisible on radar scopes is the pinnacle of critical combat and aviation technologies. Besides stealth, the fighter comes equipped with a state of the art sensor fusion capability that merges data from multiple onboard systems into a single, simplified picture for the pilot. This improves the situational awareness of the pilot, helping the individual make timely decisions in order to improve the combat effectiveness.Apart from the AN/APG-81 or AN/APG-85 radar, the aircraft's Distributed Aperture System (DAS) gives pilots a 360-degree view around the aircraft. This system lets the pilot keep a tab of the environs passively without emitting any radar waves that can be captured by radar warning receivers of adversarial fighters and thus betray the location of the otherwise stealthy fighter. Another key capability that keeps the F-35 at the top of the fighter food chain is the capability to merge data from multiple onboard systems, giving unparalleled situational awareness to the pilot. Through the multifunctional advanced data link, F-35s can interact with each other, ensuring that the pilots see the same tactical picture.Exposure to aircraft such as the F-35 is seen as valuable for the IAF as it looks to strengthen its posture against both China and Pakistan. Understanding how a fifth-generation stealth fighter operates, how it integrates sensor data and how it complicates detection for adversary radars gives Indian pilots and planners a clearer sense of what such platforms bring to a modern battlefield, at a time when China continues to expand its own stealth fighter fleet and Pakistan looks to modernise its air force with Chinese assistance. This kind of exposure also informs India's own thinking on what it wants in its upcoming Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft programme.India has had similar engagements with advanced air forces in the past, including participation in exercise Red Flag in the United States, exercise Orion in France, and exercise Pitch Black in Australia earlier this July, where IAF crews flew alongside the F-35 for the first time. Each of these exercises has helped the IAF benchmark its pilots and platforms against some of the most capable air combat training environments in the world. But what makes this exposure different is that this time, the IAF will be drawing the rules of engagement, giving it the ability to get what it seeks from the engagements that are about to get underway under the desert sun of Rajasthan.Tarang Shakti is being positioned as more than a routine training exercise. With Operation Sindoor's lessons feeding directly into its planning and a fifth-generation fighter like the F-35 flying in an Indian exercise for the first time, the drill offers the IAF a rare opportunity to test its assumptions, expose its pilots to unfamiliar technology, and prepare for the kind of high-intensity, multi-domain conflicts that officials say will define future air warfare in the region.
